ei.title: Katherine Johnson, a "Computer" Who Looked Beyond Numbers
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything — the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the "Black computers" who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and being referred to with terms like "girl" despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go. Katherine asked, "Is there a law that says I can't go?" The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division received credit as an author of a research report. Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. "If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today. Katherine retired in 1986 after thirty-three years at NASA. After that, she dedicated the rest of her life to championing access to STEM education for Black girls. For her contributions, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015 and said, "Katherine G. Johnson refused to be limited by society's expectations of her gender and race while expanding the boundaries of humanity's reach." In 2017, NASA dedicated a building in her honor in Virginia and named it the Katherine G. Johnson Computational Research Facility. She died on February 24, 2020, at the age of 101, but her pioneering legacy will never be forgotten.

④ took → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'By her junior year, she had ___ all the math courses'에서 앞에 had가 있으므로 'had + 과거분사'의 과거완료예요. 3학년 때까지 이미 수강을 '끝냈다'는 완료의 뜻이라 과거분사 taken으로 써야 해요. took(과거형)은 완료 자리에 올 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ took은 틀림 ←정답

questions.passage: Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. "If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'it made many minor errors'에서 전자 컴퓨터가 사소한 오류를 많이 냈다고 했으므로 불일치

❌ ② 본문 'Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers'와 글렌이 손 계산 재확인을 요청한 것에서 손 계산이 더 신뢰받았으므로 불일치

✅ ③ 본문 'Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations'와 일치 ←정답

❌ ④ 본문 'even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today'에서 화성 계획에도 관여했으므로 불일치
det.tip: a pencil and a slide rule ~ a day and a half checking이 일치. 나머지는 본문과 반대입니다.

ch: NASA가 사용한 전자 컴퓨터는 사소한 오류를 전혀 만들지 않았다.
글렌은 캐서린의 손 계산보다 전자 컴퓨터의 수치를 더 신뢰했다.
캐서린은 연필과 계산자만을 사용하여 하루 반 동안 계산을 확인했다.
캐서린은 아폴로 11호 계산에는 참여했지만 화성 탐사 계획에는 관여하지 않았다.

questions.passage: By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could ①<u>offer</u>. Her mentor gladly ②<u>offering</u> special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he ③<u>told</u> his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he ④<u>replied</u>, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② offering → offered: 주어 Her mentor의 정동사 자리이므로 과거시제 offered
det.analysis:
① offer: 'all the math courses the college could offer'에서 조동사 could 뒤라 동사원형 offer가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② offering → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Her mentor gladly ___ special classes just for her'에서 주어 Her mentor에 대한 정동사가 필요해요. 문맥상 '제공했다'(과거)이므로 과거시제 offered로 써야 해요. offering(분사)은 동사 자리에 올 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ offering은 틀림 ←정답

③ told: '"You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student'에서 '말했다'(과거)이므로 과거시제 told가 맞아요(tell + 목적어). ✅ 올바름

④ replied: '"That," he replied, "will be your problem."'에서 '대답했다'(과거)이므로 과거시제 replied가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 주어 + 정동사(과거 offered)

questions.passage: It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the "Black computers" who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and being referred to with terms like "girl" despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 캐서린은 백인 남성 엔지니어를 지원하기 위해 복잡한 계산을 수동으로 수행한 사람들을 가리키는 표현으로 불렸는데, 그 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'she worked as one of the "Black computers" who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers'에서 복잡한 계산을 수동으로 수행해 백인 남성 엔지니어를 지원한 사람들을 'Black computers(흑인 컴퓨터)'라고 불렀다고 했다.
det.tip: one of the "Black computers"에서 Black computers를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Katherine retired in 1986 after thirty-three years at NASA. After that, she dedicated the rest of her life to championing access to STEM education for Black girls. For her contributions, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015 and said, "Katherine G. Johnson refused to be limited by society's expectations of her gender and race while expanding the boundaries of humanity's reach." In 2017, NASA dedicated a building in her honor in Virginia and named it the Katherine G. Johnson Computational Research Facility.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 캐서린은 은퇴 후 흑인 소녀들이 어떤 교육을 받을 수 있도록 옹호하는 데 여생을 바쳤는지, 그 교육을 나타내는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'she dedicated the rest of her life to championing access to STEM education for Black girls'에서 은퇴 후 흑인 소녀들이 'STEM education(과학·기술·공학·수학 교육)'을 받을 수 있도록 옹호하는 데 여생을 바쳤다고 했다.
det.tip: championing access to STEM education에서 STEM education을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine __________ (graduate) from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 주절의 주어는 Katherine이고, 뒤에 and로 이어지는 동사 began이 과거시제다. 1935년이라는 과거 시점의 사건이고 began과 병렬을 이루므로 graduate를 과거시제 graduated로 바꿔야 한다. 'graduated from college ~ and began her career(대학을 졸업하고 경력을 시작했다)'로 해석된다.
det.tip: 과거 시점(In 1935) + began과 병렬 → graduated

questions.passage: Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything — the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 인물과 소재.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 글은 인종·성 차별을 극복하고 NASA에서 복잡한 계산과 궤도 비행 성공에 기여한 수학자 캐서린 존슨의 생애를 다룸 ← 정답

❌ ② 존 글렌의 궤도 비행은 캐서린의 업적을 보여 주는 하나의 사례일 뿐임

❌ ③ 인종 분리 교육은 그녀가 겪은 배경일 뿐 글의 주제가 아님

❌ ④ 아폴로 11호는 그녀가 참여한 프로젝트의 예시일 뿐임
det.tip: 차별을 극복한 캐서린 존슨의 삶과 업적을 관통하는 것이 주제입니다.

det.analysis:

questions.passage: Despite her enormous contributions, __________. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그 중요한 연구 회의는 백인 직원들 사이에서만 열렸다." (11단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) among, held, important, meetings, members, only, research, staff, the, were, white 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: the important research meetings were held only among white staff members
det.analysis:
주어는 '그 중요한 연구 회의'예요: the + important + research + meetings.

회의는 '열리는' 대상이라 수동태 'were + 과거분사(held)'로 써요: were + held.

'~ 사이에서만'은 only among으로 이어요: only + among.

누구 사이인가 하면 '백인 직원들'이에요: white + staff + members.

순서대로 이으면 the / important / research / meetings / were / held / only / among / white / staff / members.
det.tip: 수동태 were held + only among + 명사구(white staff members)

questions.wa: the important research meetings were held only among white staff members
accept: the important research meetings were held only among white staff members
